project.name: GVP
project.tagline: A fully on-device voice assistant for Android — speech in, speech out, no cloud calls.
project.thesis: A complete conversational voice loop (STT + a real LLM + TTS) running entirely on a stock Android phone, offline, today. Verified end-to-end in airplane mode on a Pixel 10 (Tensor G5).
headlineProofPoints: Two user-switchable on-device LLM runtimes: MediaPipe/LiteRT and Gemini Nano via AICore.
Two user-switchable on-device STT engines: Sherpa-ONNX and ML Kit GenAI ASR.
622 ms time-to-first-token on the all-AICore path (Gemini Nano LLM + ML Kit GenAI STT), Pixel 10.
User-selectable LLM model catalog (Qwen 0.5B/1.5B, Phi-4-mini, Gemma) downloaded on-device.
Live partial transcripts, VAD-bracketed utterances, and speaker-mode barge-in.
Multi-turn memory with a rolling 5-exchange window; transcripts persisted locally (Room).

architectureStyle.di: Manual DI via a ServiceLocator object (no Hilt/Dagger)
architectureStyle.state: VoiceAgentViewModel exposing StateFlow; streaming via Kotlin Flow
architectureStyle.backgroundExecution: Active listening runs in a foreground service (microphone type)
architectureStyle.networkPolicy: INTERNET permission used only for optional first-launch model download; never during the live pipeline

testedDevices: Galaxy S25 (SM-S931U1) — MediaPipe only; AICore Feature 636 returns 606-FEATURE_NOT_FOUND
Pixel 10 (Tensor G5) — AICore Gemini Nano AVAILABLE; full pipeline incl. barge-in verified

permissions.name: FOREGROUND_SERVICE
permissions.purpose: Run the mic pipeline while backgrounded

pipeline.flowDiagram: mic -> VAD -> STT -> LLM -> sanitizer -> TTS -> speaker

stages.name: Audio capture
stages.detail: 16 kHz mono PCM with a fixed 8x software gain stage. The Tensor G5 VOICE_COMMUNICATION chain delivers signal ~20-50x too quiet; the gain restores usable levels for the VAD and recognizer.

stages.name: Voice activity detection
stages.detail: Brackets utterances (speech start/end) and provides an echo-suppression gate for barge-in. Silero VAD ONNX is the planned neural upgrade behind the same interface.

stages.name: Speech-to-text
stages.engine: Sherpa-ONNX streaming Zipformer (default) OR ML Kit GenAI ASR (AICore)
stages.detail: Emits live partials; Sherpa finalizes on VAD SPEECH_END, ML Kit uses its own endpointing. Input is gated while TTS plays so neither engine transcribes the assistant's echo. Selected per-session by SttRouter.

stages.name: Near-duplicate filter
stages.detail: On VAD SPEECH_END the transcript is finalized; areSimilar() drops near-duplicate finals before sending to the LLM.

stages.name: Language model
stages.engine: MediaPipe/LiteRT (primary) OR Gemini Nano via AICore OR stub
stages.detail: Runs system message + last 5 turns + new turn through the active engine, streaming deltas to the UI plus a final completion. Engine chosen by LlmOrchestrator honoring the PipelineMode toggle.

stages.name: Speech sanitizer
stages.detail: Strips markdown, newlines, and emoji from the LLM text before it is spoken.

stages.name: Text-to-speech
stages.detail: Speaks the sanitized reply with audio focus; drives the visualizer level. System English (US) voice by default; voice is user-selectable.

stages.name: Barge-in
stages.detail: If the user speaks while TTS plays, cancels the in-flight LLM and stops TTS. 150 ms debounce + ~1.2 s TTS-onset grace; VAD uses a 60 ms sustained onset (gap-bridged 400 ms).

implementations.name: MediaPipeLlmEngine
implementations.availability: Any supported device with the .task model downloaded
implementations.notes: Creates a fresh LlmInferenceSession per turn and re-flattens rolling history; latency grows with prompt length (~0.8s -> ~2.0s). Planned: persistent KV-cache session.

implementations.name: MlKitLlmEngine
implementations.runtime: Gemini Nano via ML Kit GenAI Prompt API (AICore)
implementations.availability: Devices with ML Kit Prompt Feature 636 provisioned (e.g. Pixel 10 Tensor G5)
implementations.notes: 606-FEATURE_NOT_FOUND on non-provisioned devices is a device state, not an app bug.

implementations.name: StubLlmEngine
implementations.availability: Always — keeps the pipeline runnable when no model is present

values.behavior: MediaPipe (if model present) -> AICore Gemini Nano -> offer download -> stub
Only the selected LiteRT model; never AICore
Only Gemini Nano (Feature 636); unavailable if not provisioned

llm.defaultSystemMessage: You are a helpful voice assistant running entirely on-device. Keep responses concise and conversational — they will be spoken aloud via TTS. Limit responses to 1-3 sentences unless the user asks for detail. Never use bullet points, numbered lists, markdown, emojis, or special formatting. Speak in plain, natural sentences like a real conversation.
llm.historyWindow: Rolling 5 exchanges (system message + last 5 turns + new turn)

stt.contract: SttEngine (ownsMic, start, sendPcm, events -> Flow<SttEvent: UserStart|UserStop|Partial>, close)
stt.router: SttRouter — selects Sherpa vs ML Kit at session start from the settings toggle

implementations.name: SherpaSttEngine
implementations.notes: Fed PCM via sendPcm; VAD-gated; finalizes on VAD SPEECH_END.

implementations.name: MlKitGenAiSttEngine
implementations.notes: Fed the same PCM via an AudioSource.fromPfd pipe so VAD/barge-in/echo-suppression keep working. Prefers Basic (on-device SODA) over Advanced (nano-v3) because Advanced contends with the Gemini Nano LLM on AICore. Toggle PREFER_ADVANCED in the engine.

tts.voice: User-selectable among installed system voices; default English (US)

vad.implementation: SileroVad (energy RMS heuristic today; Silero VAD ONNX planned)
vad.params: 60 ms sustained onset, 400 ms gap-bridge, tunable end-of-utterance silence and mic-sensitivity bars

llmModelCatalog.source: GvpLlmModel.CATALOG (LlmModelSpec entries); selected in Settings -> Language model; persisted via GvpPrefs.llmModelId

hardProblems.title: Device-specific audio capture
hardProblems.problem: The Pixel 10's VOICE_COMMUNICATION + AEC/NS/AGC chain delivered signal ~20-50x too quiet (loud speech peaked ~0.013 RMS vs the 0.027 VAD bar) — no transcripts at all.
hardProblems.fix: An 8x software gain stage in AudioCapture.
hardProblems.takeaway: On-device audio is not uniform across handsets; the gain is a per-device constant.

hardProblems.title: AICore contention
hardProblems.problem: Running ML Kit GenAI Advanced ASR and Gemini Nano simultaneously both hit AICore and starve each other (Nano slowed ~2s -> >6s, replies cancelled).
hardProblems.fix: Prefer Basic (SODA) STT; keep the LLM off AICore when using Advanced ASR (PREFER_ADVANCED = false).
hardProblems.takeaway: The on-device accelerator is a shared, finite resource — you schedule around it.

hardProblems.title: Turn-taking is the frontier
hardProblems.problem: Today's VAD and barge-in are energy heuristics, not a model.
hardProblems.fix: Roadmap: a fully-on-device, Deepgram-Flux-style neural turn model.
hardProblems.takeaway: Neural VAD -> eager endpointing -> semantic end-of-turn is the path.

roadmap.detail: Replace the energy SileroVad with real Silero VAD ONNX (~2 MB, bundled with Sherpa) behind the same interface.
Flux-style eager -> resume -> commit; start the LLM on a medium-confidence endpoint and cancel on resume. Retract plumbing already exists.
Run an on-device turn model (e.g. Smart Turn v2/v3, Wav2Vec2-based) at candidate endpoints instead of the fixed 1.5 s silence timer.
Feed the TTS PCM as the echo reference (e.g. WebRTC AEC3) for robust speakerphone barge-in on devices with worse hardware AEC.
Track the noise floor so capture gain and barge-in bar stop needing per-device constants.
Keep a persistent MediaPipe session that retains the KV cache and feeds only the new user turn, flattening latency regardless of conversation depth.
